Interior restored after a break-in, before the new glass is installed

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Glass replacement is done by a glass shop. We remove the broken glass from the interior, repair the damage the break caused and coordinate with the installer you or your insurer choose.

mainEntity.name: Why not just vacuum the glass myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can get the big pieces, but tempered glass spreads into seat tracks, door panels, vents and under the carpet, and a household vacuum will not survive it. Fragments left behind come out of the vents for months and cut hands and upholstery.

mainEntity.name: Should the cleanup happen before or after the new glass?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before is better, so the installer is not sealing new glass over a dirty channel and nothing gets trapped behind the new trim. We schedule around the glass appointment.

mainEntity.name: Will insurance pay for the cleanup?

acceptedAnswer.text: When the glass broke in a covered event such as a break-in, the related interior cleanup and repair is usually part of the same claim, but your insurer decides. Our itemized estimate explains each line so the adjuster can see what was needed.
